title: Annotatio IV §.IX: Augustine (1) — Institution words figurative; metonymy; Doctr. Chr. 2.16
pass_a_gloss: But the LATTER, about to utter every divine Truth on this point, (1) pronounces clearly enough that the Essential Institution words of the Sacred Supper — Take, eat, This is my Body — are figurative and not to be received without the trope of Metonymy, when against Adimantus Book 12 he writes thus: The Lord did not hesitate to say, This is my body, when He was giving a sign of His body, with reason further annexed in Book 2 On Christian Doctrine ch. 16, on account of which in Christ’s command about eating His body and in similar sayings a Figure must necessarily be understood underneath; if, says Augustine, a preceptive utterance seems to order a crime or outrage, or to forbid a usefulness or benefit, it is figurative. Unless you shall have eaten, says Christ, the flesh of the Son of Man and drunk His blood, you will not have Life in you — it seems to order a crime or outrage; IT IS THEREFORE A FIGURE, commanding that one must communicate in the Lord’s Passion and sweetly and usefully lay up in memory that His flesh was crucified and wounded for us.
pass_b_english: Augustine (1): the essential Institution words (‘Take, eat, This is my Body’) are figurative — not without metonymy (Against Adimantus 12; Doctr. Chr. 2.16).
If a command seems to order a crime, it is figurative: ‘Unless you eat my flesh…’ seems criminal — therefore it is a FIGURE commanding communion in the Passion and memory of the crucified flesh.
source_text: POSTERIOR verò, Veritatem in hoc puncto divinam omnem elocuturus (1) Verba Institutionis S. Cœnæ Essentialia: Accipite edite, Hoc est Corpus meum, figurata esse, nec sine Metonymiæ tropo accipienda, satis clarè pronuntiat, quando contra Adimantum Lib. 12. ita scribit: Dominus non dubitavit dicere, Hoc est corpus meum, cum signum daret corporis sui, subnexa insuper ratione Lib. 2. de Doctrina Christ. c. 16., ob quam in mandato Christi, de manducando corpore suo, aliisque similibus, Figura necessariò subintelligenda sit; si, inquit Augustinus, præceptiva locutio aut flagitium aut facinus videtur jubere, aut utilitatem aut beneficium vetare, figurata est. Nisi manducaveritis, inquit Christus, carnem Filii Hominis & sanguinem biberitis, non habebitis Vitam in vobis, facinus vel flagitium videtur jubere, FIGURA EST ERGO, præcipiens, Passioni Domini esse communicandum & suaviter atque utiliter recondendum in memoria, quod pro nobis caro ejus crucifixa & vulnerata est.
